To maximize the total reward in a 3-armed bandit problem, the optimal strategy involves balancing exploration (trying unknown arms) and exploitation (pulling the arm with the highest observed mean).

Since you have three arms and have only sampled one, it is statistically beneficial to explore the remaining two arms at least once to determine their potential, even though one arm has already shown a positive result.
